title: The Frog Prince.
lines: Once upon a time there was a king who had a very beautiful daughter.
The youngest princess was so beautiful that even the sun was amazed when it shone on her face.
Behind the castle was a big, dark forest.
And in that forest, under an old tree, there was a well.
A deep well, with cool, clear water.
On warm days the princess went to play there.
She always took her favourite toy with her.
A golden ball.
She threw the ball up and caught it again.
Up and catch.
Up and catch.
One day she threw the ball very high.
She missed it.
And the golden ball rolled across the ground, straight into the well.
Splash!
The princess looked into the well.
The water was so deep that she couldn't see the bottom.
Her golden ball was gone.
She began to cry.
She cried louder and louder.
Then she heard a voice.
Why are you crying so, princess?
She looked around.
There was nobody there.
Only a frog.
A fat, green frog, poking its head out of the water.
I'm crying because my golden ball fell into the well, sobbed the princess.
I can get it for you, croaked the frog.
But what will I get for it?
Anything you want!
said the princess.
My clothes, my pearls, my jewels, even my little golden crown!
The frog shook its head.
I don't want any of that.
I want you to be my friend.
To let me sit next to you at the table.
To let me eat from your little golden plate.
And to let me sleep in your bed.
Do you promise?
Yes, yes, I promise, said the princess quickly.
But meanwhile she thought: What is that silly frog talking about.
He can never get out of that well.
The frog dived down.
A little later he came back with the golden ball in his mouth.
He threw it onto the grass.
The princess grabbed her ball and ran away, back to the castle.
Wait!
called the frog.
Take me with you!
But the princess didn't listen.
The next evening the princess was sitting at the table with the king.
They were eating soup from golden plates.
Then they heard something on the stairs.
Splish, splash, splish, splash.
There was a knock at the door.
Princess, princess, open the door!
The princess went to look.
There sat the frog.
She got a fright and slammed the door shut.
Who was that?
asked the king.
The princess told him everything.
The king looked very serious.
What you promise, you must also do, he said.
Let him in.
The princess had to open the door.
The frog hopped inside.
Put me on the table, he said.
The princess did it, pulling a face.
The frog ate from her golden plate.
He smacked his lips.
The princess hardly ate anything.
After dinner the frog said: I'm tired.
Take me to your room.
The princess began to cry.
She thought the cold, wet frog was so yucky.
But the king said: He helped you when you were sad.
Now you must help him too.
The princess carried the frog upstairs.
She put him on a cushion in a corner.
But then something wonderful happened.
The frog began to grow.
He grew bigger and bigger.
His green skin became a beautiful cloak.
And suddenly there stood a prince!
A young prince with kind eyes.
A wicked witch had put a spell on me, he said.
Only a princess who kept her promise could save me.
Thank you.
The princess was ashamed.
I wasn't nice to you, she said.
I'm sorry.
The prince smiled.
You kept your promise.
That's what counts.
They became the best of friends.
Later they got married and lived happily ever after.
And the golden ball?
They played with it together, by the well in the forest.
The end.
